articles.title: Met chief Rowley not fit for job, says detective raped by colleague
articles.summary: Det Con Linda Williams, a victim of serial abuser David Carrick, says she has no faith in the system.
articles.body:
A Met Police detective who was raped by a fellow officer has said the force's handling of her case was "like being raped all over again".

Det Con Linda Williams was attacked in 2004 by PC David Carrick - who was jailed for life in 2023 for sexual offences against her and 11 others.

Linda sought damages from the Met for failing to protect her from Carrick and said the process left her feeling suicidal.

She now wants Met Commissioner, Sir Mark Rowley, to resign because he has failed to change police culture as promised.

articles.title: Amid attacks, sales surge at Kolkata Left book stalls
articles.summary: Left bookstall sales near Durga Puja pandals surge in Kolkata despite vandalism attempts; CPM’s Jadavpur stall hits Rs 16 lakh; HC case filed.
articles.body: KOLKATA: Book sales at stalls set up near Durga Puja pandals by various Left parties—including the CPM, CPI(ML) Liberation, and SUCI—spiked manifold this year, coinciding with reports of vandalism, arson, and books being thrown onto the streets across the city and the state.At the Jadavpur 8B bus stand, where a bulldozer attempted to demolish book stalls on Saturday before facing resistance from locals, the CPM stall recorded sales worth Rs 16 lakh—a nearly fourfold increase from last year’s Rs 4.5 lakh. Meanwhile, the stall set up by the All India Students’ Association (AISA) at the same location recorded sales of Rs 80,000, up from Rs 50,000 last year, according to AISA state president Ritam Maji.The only total casualty was the SUCI (Communist) stall, which was pulled down around midnight. However, its sales still surged after volunteers resumed operations using makeshift tables and chairs. The Jadavpur SUCI stall sold books worth Rs 75,000, compared to Rs 55,000 in 2025. The APDR moved the Calcutta High Court on Thursday against the demolition of a book stall near Jadavpur Super Market, demanding accountability and compensation; the matter will be heard on October 29.CPI(ML) Liberation was not allowed to set up its stall at Dhakuria. However, party sources said books worth Rs 25,000 were sold from its Moulali stall—almost double last year’s figures. CPM state committee member Sudip Sengupta said: “Despite the attacks on bookstalls, we have noticed a surge in sales. Apart from the Jadavpur 8B bus stand stall, our stall at Bagbazar Sarbajonin also received a great response, generating Rs 4.5 lakh this year compared to around Rs 1.5 lakh last year. At Bijoygarh, books worth Rs 1.3 lakh were sold, while our Netaji Nagar stall generated Rs 2.2 lakh.”Kallol Majumdar, CPM Kolkata district secretary, said that out of 119 bookstalls set up by the CPM in Kolkata this Puja, over 30 faced disruptions or were vandalised. Stalls were attacked in Rashbehari, Lake Market, Behala, Haridevpur, Nagerbazar, Boral, Howrah, and Siliguri, among other places, he added.A video from Nagerbazar went viral on social media showing right-wing supporters vandalising a CPM stall and throwing books—including Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay’s Pather Dabi—onto the ground.Seventy-three-year-old Bipul Dasgupta, a CPM whole-timer, was seen urging the youths to flip through the pages before discarding them, but his pleas fell on deaf ears.SUCI (Communist) state secretary Chandidas Bhattacharya said: “Despite attacks on hundreds of stalls across districts, overall sales have increased by 40% to 50% compared to last year.”Senior BJP and RSS leaders have also spoken out against damaging books.BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said no genuine party worker could carry out such an act, emphasizing that the vandalism of Left bookstalls cannot be supported under any circumstances. State finance minister Swapan Dasgupta remarked: “If it were an isolated incident, I could understand; but the fact that the same thing happened in three or four places makes me bow my head in shame.” Bengal RSS spokesperson Jishnu Basu said: “Those who destroy bookstalls to display muscle power do not understand India, its culture of tolerance and acceptance, or its commitment to freedom of expression.”Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari also weighed in on the debate. “We are not against books. However, those who do not follow Sanatani rituals or participate in Durga Puja still set up stalls near the pandals. The police and KMC acted in accordance with the order issued by the Calcutta High Court. I appeal to everyone not to take the law into their own hands. This party has already lost its relevance; do not do anything that makes them relevant again,” he said.Adhikari added that Left parties should sell their literature from inside their party offices. “It is better not to allow those who do not believe in Durga Puja—or any puja for that matter—and who do not acknowledge the Vedas, Upanishads, and Gita, to sell books during the festival. Keep your books inside the party office. Whoever wants information can go there and get it.”Trinamool Congress MLA Kunal Ghosh and West Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar, visited the Left stalls to express solidarity and buy books.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Only ‘sanatanis’ will touch idols during immersion: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari
articles.summary: Suvendu Adhikari says only ‘Sanatan Dharma’ believers may touch Durga idols during immersion; police to record names; opposition calls it exclusionary.
articles.body: KOLKATA: Only those who believe in ‘sanatan dharma’ will be allowed to touch Durga idols during immersion, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Wednesday while inspecting security arrangements at Baje Kadamtala Ghat. Dismissing suggestions that the directive had a communal intent, Adhikari said the measure was aimed at upholding the sanctity of immersion rituals.Adhikari said Kolkata Police commissioner Ajay Nand has been instructed to maintain a record of those involved in immersion. “Only those who believe in Sanatan Dharma should touch the idols. I have told the CP to record the names of those who come here. They must also be identified,” the CM said. “To preserve sanctity, we must follow traditions, scriptures and norms followed for thousands of years,” he added.The CM’s remarks drew strong reactions, with opposition netas accusing him of promoting religious exclusion and violating constitutional principles.“Does he (Adhikari) have a list of who is a ‘sanatani’ and who is not? Can he explain how someone becomes a ‘sanatani’? He has no answers,” former CPM MP Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya said. He also alleged that the CM was acting in accordance with the RSS agenda.Bengal Congress senior Suman Roy Chaudhuri condemned Adhikari’s remarks, arguing that they ran contrary to India’s constitutional commitment to pluralism.Trinamool’s Baiswanor Chatterjee criticised the CM, saying, “One cannot understand Hinduism with such a narrow mindset.”Earlier, citing traditions, Adhikari had said trolleys, and not cranes, would be used in immersions and DJ music would be banned. On Wednesday, cranes were out and rail-mounted trolleys took their place at immersions in Hooghly. Special mechanical ramps, trolleys and conveyor systems have been installed at major immersion ghats like Baje Kadamtala, Nimtala and Gwalior ghat.Blaring loudspeakers, unlike in previous years, were absent. In some pockets, however, fireworks shattered the relative quiet.Environment activist Naba Dutta of Sabuj Mancha said, “We have been protesting the use of DJ music, but for the first time, our wishes have been fulfilled.”Sources at KMC confirmed that around 2,800 idols were immersed on Wednesday. While Doighat recorded immersion of around 700 idols, Baje Kadamtala recorded 560 immersions. Nimtala and Judges Ghat saw a surge in immersions. A majority of puja organisers stayed away from immersions.On Thursday afternoon, however, a TOI team saw heaps of idol structures at Baje Kadamtala Ghat. Holding low tide responsible for this, a KMC official said, “We are waiting for high tide to clear the accumulated structures.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Caldey Island monk gave naked photos of himself to visitors
articles.summary: The monk denies sexually assaulting a visitor, who says he also gave her naked photos of himself.
articles.body:
A woman has spoken out for the first time about an alleged sexual assault by a monk who lived on a private island off the coast of west Wales.

Brother Titus Keet, 78, has also been accused of sexually harassing and sexually assaulting a former Caldey Island employee as well as giving women naked photos of himself.

He denied the allegations saying "a woman who feels rejected can become very vicious" and said the pictures were not sexual, but he would reflect on his behaviour.

The claims, revealed in a new BBC podcast Dark Island , were investigated by Dyfed-Powys Police but there was no further action.

Caldey Island is off the coast of Tenby, Pembrokeshire, and is owned by a group of Cistercian monks.

Single mum Natalie Roberts was a regular visitor from the early 2000s and would spend holidays there with her two sons.

She told the Dark Island podcast that Keet would give her photos of himself posing naked on beaches on Caldey, often accompanied by a poem.

In 2016, Natalie went for a walk from Caldey to nearby St Margaret's Island with her sons and a friend.

The walk is quite dangerous and you have to scramble across slippery rocks to get from one island to the other.

Natalie claims it was then, when Keet was walking behind her, he repeatedly sexually assaulted her over her clothes.

She said she was horrified, adding: "I was so angry because I knew this was an absolute violation.

"You know, this wasn't spiritual. This was his opportunity just to do that."

She said she was stunned but did not say anything to Keet because she thought he would deny it and she might be asked to leave the island.

Natalie said: "I think the worst thing it did, if I'm completely honest, it took away my whole spiritual belief in Catholicism."

But Keet claimed she turned "wickedly against him" after he rejected her attempts to seduce him.

It is also claimed Keet made several unwelcome sexual advances towards an employee of the abbey.

Allegedly, he touched her breasts and bottom, commented on her body and referred to her genitals, despite being asked not to.

Other allegations included making sexualised comments while showing nude photos of himself and pictures of naked women.

It is claimed Keet was confronted at the time but said UK law did not apply to him as he was a Dutch citizen, that he could do as he liked as he was on a private island and allegedly, he called the employee "too sensitive".

He is also accused of saying the woman was lucky to receive sexual attention from him and "women welcomed male attention".

It is also claimed the monk told her she would lose her job if she complained.

Keet said the allegations were false and quoted The Bible in his statement to the podcast: "To all who are pure themselves, everything is pure; but to those who have been corrupted and lack faith, nothing can be pure [Letter to Titus 1,15]."

He said the employee had made up the allegations in the hope the monastery would pay her money and that she was paid to "keep quiet".

"If it was not so sad, it would be laughable, how she could make up so many allegations spread out over three years, in which we had co-operated so pleasantly together. Very sad," he added.

In response to the allegation from Natalie, he said: "This is a classic example of a woman who felt frustrated in her advances, disappointed in her expectations, feeling rejected and then turns against the other in a very vicious way."

Natalie denied that claim and said he was in a position of "significant power" and she was in a position of vulnerability.

She added he used victim-blaming language and had attempted to discredit her.

The abbot of Caldey Abbey, Father Jan Rossey, said they referred complaints in line with their safeguarding procedures.

He said in 2024, Keet was "required to leave" Caldey Island and will not be allowed back.

This was years after the employee made a complaint of sexual assault.

About 50,000 day trippers catch the boat from the popular seaside resort of Tenby to visit Caldey island every year.

It is owned by the order of monks that live there, and is only 1.5 miles (2.4km) long and a mile (1.6km) wide.

Visitors who stay overnight can do so in the guesthouse or other properties the monks own.

There are also about 30 lay people who live there.

Caldey Island was once known for being "crime free", but in 2017, six women settled a civil claim against the abbey .

The former abbot Robert O'Brien knew about the abuse but did not report it.

An independent review, published in 2024, found that victims were treated in a heartless, hostile and cruel way.

It said frequent allegations of abuse were made, but not followed up on or reported to police, and the lack of challenge had enabled Kotik to abuse children over four decades "in plain sight".

Other offenders have also stayed on the island, including a man who was wanted by police and lived under an alias for seven years before being jailed for 30 months for possessing child abuse images.

The abuse by Kotik was investigated by the police in 2014 and 2017, but officers concluded there was little they could do as he died in 1992.

However, a former head of crime for the force has called for a renewed investigation into the abuse by Kotik, which could also look at how three other offenders - Paul Ashton, John Cronin and John Shannon - came to stay on the island.

Steve Wilkins, who led the operation behind the conviction of serial killer John Cooper, said: "Was the magnet that drew them there that they could go and hide in plain sight?

"They could continue their offending with little chance of it being reported to the authorities."

Dyfed-Powys Police said it had followed all appropriate lines of enquiry and there were no ongoing investigations.

Rossey apologised and acknowledged child abuse was previously ignored.

He said it was deeply concerning people felt unable to speak up or feared exclusion if they raised concerns.

He said things had changed on the island, that new safeguarding measures had been introduced including a committee with police, council staff and a survivor of abuse.

People who live and work on the island must now have criminal record checks, original ID and have interviews with the abbot and island manager.

He said the abbey was committed to openness, listening to those harmed and learning from past failures.

He said all recommendations from an independent review into abuse on the island had been implemented.

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'Prepare for the worst' and 'Covid report fallout'
articles.summary: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting's national campaign on preparedness for cyber or climate emergencies dominates today's papers.
articles.body:
Spoiler warning: This review reveals details from the latest episodes of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.

The Sun reports that Thomas Markle, the estranged father of the Duchess of Sussex, is being investigated by police, after a "huge stash" of child sex abuse images was allegedly found at his home in the Philippines. The paper reports that the discovery was made by the 82-year-old's son, Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Junior. It says he told detectives that "hundreds, if not thousands" of pictures and videos of young girls were "mixed up with innocent family mementos" in four large boxes. There is no response from Thomas Markle Senior.

A number of the papers lead on government warnings about preparing for national emergencies. The Guardian says there is "growing concern" about the impact of climate change, technological dependency and hostile state threats, with the Daily Telegraph highlighting Britain's reliance on undersea cables and a "heavily globalised food supply". But the Daily Mail dismisses the warnings , accusing what it calls "Nanny Burnham" of "wasting a fortune on lecturing" the country. Its headline is: "Don't panic."

The Times says that the government is to make its revived Help to Buy scheme "more generous" by raising the earnings cap on who can qualify. It says first-time buyers outside London with a combined income of up to £110,000 will be able to access the scheme, up from £90,000 pounds. In the capital, the threshold is being raised to £140,00 pounds, from £110,000.

The Financial Times says that Nato will allow Ukraine to buy weapons, ammunition and equipment through its centralised procurement agency. The paper says this could potentially allow Kyiv to obtain supplies faster and more cheaply, and without having to rely on bilateral negotiations.

And reports that the search for the next James Bond is nearing its end are highlighted in the Times . It says that among the final contenders are the Slow Horses' star, Jack Lowden; Callum Turner from Masters of the Air; and Josh O'Connor, who played Prince Charles in The Crown. They - along with up to two others - are said to be gathering in London this weekend for screen tests. The paper says the next 007 is set to be recruited before the end of the year.

images.caption: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has made headlines in today's papers after launching a national campaign on public preparedness for disruption caused by natural disasters and cyber attacks. The Daily Telegraph reports on Britons being asked to make "Be ready" kits for emergencies, "including three days' worth of non-perishable food and bottled water, an FM radio and blankets".

articles.title: Negociar com patrão e mais: o que Lula e Flávio propõem ao trabalhador | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidatos divergem sobre o futuro do trabalho: Flávio defende contratos mais flexíveis e negociação direta, enquanto Lula propõe a ampliação da proteção social. Entenda o que está em jogo.
articles.summary: Redução da jornada, flexibilidade nos contratos e direitos para trabalhadores de aplicativos estão entre as propostas que podem afetar a rotina e a renda de milhões de brasileiros.
articles.body:
Fim da escala 6x1: como empresas antecipam mudanças na jornada de trabalho na região de Campinas — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

O debate sobre emprego e modelos de trabalho ganhou espaço nos programas de governo, nas declarações públicas e nas propostas dos candidatos à Presidência da República.

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) , candidato à reeleição, defende a preservação e o fortalecimento da Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT), marco das relações trabalhistas brasileiras desde 1943.

Já Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) considera que a CLT não acompanha parte das transformações ocorridas no mundo do trabalho nas últimas décadas e defende uma revisão das regras, com medidas como a adoção de contratos por hora e maior peso para as negociações entre empresas e trabalhadores.

💬 Veja abaixo o que se discute sobre a vida dos trabalhadores. Ao fim da reportagem, confira os posicionamentos de cada candidato sobre o tema.

A CLT nasceu em 1943, durante o governo de Getúlio Vargas, em um momento em que o Brasil avançava na industrialização e buscava estruturar suas relações de trabalho.

Ao longo das décadas, a legislação incorporou uma série de garantias, como férias remuneradas, 13º salário, FGTS, licença-maternidade e regras sobre a jornada de trabalho. A carteira assinada passou a representar, para sucessivas gerações, a porta de entrada para esses direitos.

Mas o mercado de trabalho mudou. A indústria perdeu participação na economia, enquanto o setor de serviços ganhou espaço.

Com o avanço da internet, surgiram novas formas de contratação, plataformas digitais passaram a intermediar novas atividades e milhões de trabalhadores passaram a atuar por conta própria, como microempreendedores ou pessoas jurídicas.

Os dados são frequentemente utilizados por candidatos e grupos que defendem mudanças na legislação trabalhista. O argumento é que as transformações no mercado exigem relações de trabalho mais flexíveis.

O que divide os candidatos é a forma como interpretam essas mudanças e, principalmente, o que propõem diante delas.

Para Flávio, a expansão dessas modalidades mostra que a legislação trabalhista se tornou excessivamente rígida e precisa abrir espaço para relações mais livres entre empresas e trabalhadores.

Para Lula, as mesmas transformações mostram a necessidade de atualizar os mecanismos de proteção social para quem já não está inserido nas formas tradicionais de emprego.

O discurso que contesta os ganhos da CLT se intensificou nos últimos anos, especialmente nas redes sociais:

A carteira assinada passou a ser associada a jornadas rígidas, longos deslocamentos, baixos salários e pouca autonomia.

Por outro lado, a informalidade, o empreendedorismo e o trabalho por conta própria costumam ser apresentados como símbolos de liberdade, independência e possibilidade de ascensão financeira.

Para o sociólogo Ricardo Antunes, muitos jovens cresceram vendo pais e familiares enfrentarem rotinas exaustivas de trabalho sem alcançar estabilidade financeira ou uma melhora significativa de vida.

Ao mesmo tempo, foram expostos a uma cultura que valoriza o empreendedorismo individual e a ideia de autonomia profissional.

"A promessa de 'ser o próprio chefe' passou a exercer forte apelo, especialmente em um contexto marcado pelo avanço das plataformas digitais e das novas tecnologias. Mas existe uma diferença importante entre a promessa de autonomia e a realidade desses trabalhadores."

A cientista política Mayra Goulart afirma que muitos trabalhadores buscam mais liberdade para organizar o próprio tempo e construir relações menos hierárquicas. Isso não significa, porém, que tenham condições de negociar livremente sua sobrevivência econômica.

"Ele não está numa posição em que consegue, de fato, gerenciar o seu tempo. Não consegue, de fato, gerenciar o seu descanso, porque precisa lutar pela sua sobrevivência, precisa batalhar pela sua dignidade."

Na avaliação da pesquisadora, esse cenário se conecta a uma visão que transforma a precarização em virtude.

"Há a proliferação de uma ideologia em que essa luta pela dignidade, muitas vezes, leva à superexploração, à autoexploração desse empreendedor de si mesmo, que trabalha horas sem descanso, não tira férias ou trabalha machucado. Isso passa a ser visto como uma virtude moral."

Por que os diagnósticos são tão diferentes?

Para Mayra Goulart, a resposta passa por divergências mais profundas sobre liberdade econômica, desigualdade social e o papel do Estado. Segundo ela, parte das críticas à legislação trabalhista está associada à ideia de que a regulação estatal limita a liberdade econômica.

Na prática, a divergência entre as ideias dos candidatos aparece na forma como cada grupo enxerga a relação entre trabalhadores e empregadores.

Os defensores da flexibilização argumentam que o mercado se tornou dinâmico demais para continuar submetido a regras pensadas para uma realidade industrial do século passado. Para eles, ampliar a liberdade contratual ajudaria a gerar empregos e atender às demandas de trabalhadores que buscam mais autonomia.

Já os defensores da manutenção ou ampliação dos direitos trabalhistas partem de outra premissa: trabalhadores e empresas não negociam em condições equivalentes e, por isso, precisam existir garantias mínimas protegidas por lei.

A cientista política afirma que essa discussão se tornou mais complexa porque as transformações tecnológicas avançaram mais rapidamente do que os mecanismos de proteção social conseguiram se adaptar.

"Há uma certa dificuldade de adaptar as ideologias trabalhistas tradicionais a essas novas tecnologias e aos novos tempos, sem abrir mão da ideia de que esse trabalhador não está numa relação de igualdade com as elites econômicas."

Os números do mercado de trabalho mostram que, apesar do debate sobre a carteira assinada, o emprego formal continua crescendo no país.

Dados divulgados pelo Ministério do Trabalho mostram que o Brasil criou 165,8 mil vagas com carteira assinada apenas em agosto. Com isso, o saldo acumulado do ano chegou a mais de 1,1 milhão de empregos formais .

A taxa de desemprego caiu para 5,3%, o menor nível para o período na série histórica do IBGE. A população ocupada atingiu 103,5 milhões de pessoas , e o número de trabalhadores com carteira assinada no setor privado chegou a 39,5 milhões , dois recordes.

Os dados indicam que, apesar do crescimento dos aplicativos, da pejotização e do trabalho por conta própria, a carteira assinada segue sendo uma forma importante de inserção no mercado de trabalho brasileiro.

Para Ricardo Antunes, a principal discussão não é se o país deve manter exatamente a mesma legislação criada em 1943 ou substituí-la integralmente. O desafio, segundo ele, é definir quais direitos devem acompanhar os trabalhadores nas novas formas de ocupação surgidas nas últimas décadas.

Mayra Goulart propõe uma reflexão sobre quais garantias a sociedade considera indispensáveis. "Quando pensamos nessas propostas, precisamos perguntar: esse trabalhador estará protegido em caso de doença? Em caso de velhice? Quantas horas ele vai trabalhar?"

No fim das contas, o que está em disputa é como o Brasil pretende responder a uma pergunta que acompanha as transformações do mundo do trabalho: quem deve assumir os riscos da vida profissional em uma economia cada vez mais flexível?

Lula (à esq) e Flávio Bolsonaro (à dir) participaram de sabatinas na TV Globo — Foto: Divulgação

Veja o que diz o plano de governo dos candidatos

Flávio Bolsonaro afirma que não pretende acabar com a CLT nem retirar direitos trabalhistas. Sua proposta é ampliar a liberdade de negociação entre trabalhadores e empresas , especialmente em relação à jornada de trabalho. O candidato também defende modelos mais flexíveis de contratação.

Seu coordenador de campanha, o senador Rogério Marinho (PL), é autor de uma PEC que cria um regime alternativo de trabalho por hora. A proposta ainda tramita no Senado e seus defensores afirmam que a discussão deve avançar após as eleições.

Segundo o candidato, muitas pessoas gostariam de trabalhar mais horas para aumentar a renda ou adotar escalas mais adequadas à própria rotina, mas encontram limitações nas regras atuais.

Outro ponto defendido é o fortalecimento do chamado "negociado sobre o legislado", permitindo que empregado e empregador definam determinadas condições de trabalho por acordo direto . Para o candidato, relações mais flexíveis podem gerar mais oportunidades de emprego e acomodar melhor diferentes perfis de trabalhadores.

Lula defende a preservação e o fortalecimento da proteção trabalhista. Seu programa parte do diagnóstico de que houve precarização das relações de trabalho nos últimos anos e propõe ampliar direitos e garantias para trabalhadores formais e informais.

Entre as principais propostas estão a manutenção da política de valorização do salário mínimo, a redução da jornada semanal para 40 horas, o apoio ao fim da escala 6x1 e a regulamentação do trabalho por aplicativos, com previsão de contribuição previdenciária, proteção social e regras permanentes para o setor.

O candidato também defende o combate à pejotização considerada irregular, o fortalecimento da negociação coletiva e da atuação sindical, além da ampliação de políticas de crédito para microempreendedores, autônomos e cooperativas.

O g1 procurou as campanhas dos candidatos para detalhar suas propostas e esclarecer pontos relacionados às mudanças que defendem para as relações de trabalho.

A seguir, veja a íntegra das manifestações enviadas pelas assessorias.

Ao contrário do que tentam distorcer ou criticar, Flávio Bolsonaro defende a liberdade para que trabalhador e empregador escolham a melhor carga horária para ambos como destaca o eixo “O Brasil que Prospera”, do seu plano de governo “Para o Brasil Vencer o Atraso”.

Para o candidato à presidência, a pessoa não tem que ficar engessada com uma escala fixa que não vai resolver a vida dela. Na avaliação de Flávio, “quem quiser trabalhar no sistema que está, vai continuar, mas vai ter a possibilidade de trabalhar, com todos os direitos trabalhistas garantidos, com a jornada que for possível. Se quiser trabalhar mais horas, vai trabalhar também e vai ganhar mais. Vamos dar liberdade para que as pessoas possam escolher a sua carga horária de trabalho”.

O eixo “O Brasil que Prospera” apoia o negociado sobre o legislado, ou seja, a liberdade para que trabalhador e empresa combinem diretamente as condições de trabalho que funcionam para os dois, dentro da lei, em vez de seguir uma regra única imposta a todos. “Quando as duas partes negociam pensando em ganhos mútuos, cresce a qualidade do emprego, crescem as empresas e crescem as oportunidades”, traz o candidato em seu plano de governo.

Procurada, a campanha de Lula não respondeu ao pedido de declaração.

articles.title: Plano de Trump para Itaipu pode reduzir energia para o Brasil; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Aumento do consumo de energia no Paraguai pode diminuir o excedente destinado ao mercado brasileiro. Acordo entre empresas americana e paraguaia prevê construção de centro de inteligência artificial abastecido pela hidrelétrica a partir de 2027.
articles.summary: Aumento do consumo de energia no Paraguai pode diminuir o excedente destinado ao mercado brasileiro. Acordo entre empresas americana e paraguaia prevê construção de centro de IA.
articles.body:
O plano anunciado pelo governo de Donald Trump para utilizar energia da usina de Itaipu, na fronteira entre Brasil e Paraguai, para abastecer empresas de inteligência artificial pode reduzir a quantidade de eletricidade destinada ao mercado brasileiro nos próximos anos. O alerta é de especialistas em energia ouvidos pelo g1 , após o anúncio de uma parceria entre uma empresa americana e uma empresa paraguaia nesta quarta-feira (21).

Segundo os pesquisadores, o Paraguai tem ampliado o consumo da energia que lhe pertence na hidrelétrica binacional. Com a instalação de novos empreendimentos de grande porte, a tendência é que o país utilize uma parcela cada vez maior da eletricidade e diminua o excedente atualmente disponibilizado ao Brasil.

➡️ Pelo Tratado de Itaipu, Brasil e Paraguai têm direito, cada um, à metade da energia produzida pela usina. O acordo prevê que a parcela não utilizada por um dos países seja disponibilizada para ser comprada pelo outro. Historicamente, o Paraguai consumia apenas uma pequena parte da energia a que tinha direito e destinava o excedente ao Brasil. Atualmente, o país utiliza cerca de 74% da sua metade, enquanto os 26% restantes são destinados ao mercado brasileiro.

O acordo anunciado pelos Estados Unidos envolve a empresa americana Crusoe, que desenvolve infraestrutura para inteligência artificial, e a desenvolvedora de projetos de energia e infraestrutura paraguaia Araico. A previsão é que a primeira fase do empreendimento entre em operação em meados de 2027.

Delegação americana visita a Usina de Itaipu, na fronteira entre o Brasil e o Paraguai — Foto: Embaixada dos EUA no Paraguai

O projeto utilizará energia produzida por Itaipu para abastecer uma estrutura de processamento de dados instalada no Paraguai . Segundo o governo americano, a instalação atenderá clientes dos Estados Unidos e da América Latina. O anúncio não detalhou a quantidade de energia que será contratada.

O Brasil não participou das negociações anunciadas pelo governo americano . Ao g1 , Itaipu informou que não participou do encontro entre as autoridades e que a utilização da energia destinada a cada país é uma decisão nacional, conforme as regras do tratado binacional.

Para Victorio Oxilia, doutor em Energia e professor da Faculdade Politécnica da Universidade Nacional de Assunção, no Paraguai, a redução do excedente destinado pelo lado paraguaio ao Brasil já está em andamento e pode se acelerar com a chegada de novos consumidores.

"O que dá para prever é que talvez a quantidade disponível de energia para o Brasil diminua bastante. É muito difícil que suma totalmente, mas vai diminuir bastante", afirma Oxilia.

O especialista explica que o crescimento da demanda paraguaia se intensificou a partir de 2021 e 2022, principalmente pela instalação de empresas que utilizam grandes quantidades de eletricidade, como as dedicadas à mineração de criptomoedas .

Itaipu está com duas calhas do vertedouro abertas — Foto: Itaipu Binacional

O professor de Relações Internacionais da Universidade Federal da Grande Dourados (UFGD), Tomaz Espósito, também considera que os empreendimentos podem reduzir a disponibilidade de energia para o Brasil e tornar mais complexas as negociações entre os países.

"Com um novo consumidor, as negociações do Anexo C se tornarão mais complexas , pois o Paraguai poderá ter outros consumidores, como essas empresas. No curto prazo, isso significa uma possibilidade de redução da oferta de energia ao mercado brasileiro", explica.

⚡ O Anexo C do Tratado de Itaipu estabelece as regras financeiras e de comercialização da energia produzida pela hidrelétrica, compartilhada entre Brasil e Paraguai. O documento define, entre outros pontos, como são calculados os custos da eletricidade e a compensação paga pela energia que um país não utiliza e disponibiliza ao outro.

Brasil não corre risco de desabastecimento

Apesar da possibilidade de redução, os especialistas não apontam risco imediato de desabastecimento no Brasil. Oxilia avalia que o país possui um sistema elétrico diversificado, com outras fontes de geração capazes de reduzir os impactos.

"O Brasil vai sentir essa redução de energia disponível, porém tem um sistema tão grande, com tantas opções hoje em dia, que esse impacto vai ser mínimo", afirma.

Espósito, por outro lado, chama atenção para a importância da energia de Itaipu no abastecimento do Centro-Sul brasileiro .

"Ainda que o Brasil tenha um superávit de energia, com grande potencial solar, uma reserva importante de energia do Centro-Sul vai diminuir ao longo do tempo."

Ainda não há uma estimativa oficial de quanto o empreendimento poderá reduzir a energia disponibilizada ao Brasil, nem confirmação de eventuais impactos na conta de luz dos consumidores brasileiros.

Os presidentes do Paraguai, Santiago Peña, e dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump — Foto: Reuters

O acordo para a instalação da estrutura de computação faz parte de uma série de iniciativas anunciadas pelo Departamento de Estado para ampliar os investimentos americanos no Paraguai .

Segundo o governo americano, durante a visita de Landau, uma delegação empresarial dos EUA discutiu oportunidades em setores como tecnologia, minerais críticos, infraestrutura fluvial e logística.

Além do projeto ligado a Itaipu, a empresa americana Uranium Energy Corp. anunciou um investimento de US$ 12 milhões para desenvolver uma de suas concessão de urânio no Paraguai.

Na área de segurança, os dois governos também assinaram um acordo de assistência para interceptação aérea. A iniciativa pretende ampliar a capacidade paraguaia de monitorar e proteger o espaço aéreo contra voos suspeitos de transportar drogas.

Os Estados Unidos anunciaram ainda US$ 5,5 milhões em assistência para ações contra o financiamento do terrorismo, o combate ao narcotráfico e o reforço da segurança nas fronteiras.

Outros US$ 6,25 milhões serão destinados à cooperação bilateral contra o crime organizado transnacional.

Os dois países também iniciaram negociações para estabelecer um acordo de cooperação no uso pacífico da energia nuclear.

Se o entendimento entrar em vigor, será criado um marco legal para permitir que empresas americanas exportem equipamentos e materiais nucleares para o Paraguai, sob regras de segurança e não proliferação.

articles.standfirst: A data celebra o serviço público federal, mas a folga depende das regras de cada estado e município. Trabalhadores da iniciativa privada não têm direito à dispensa; veja os próximos feriados do ano.
articles.summary: A data celebra o serviço público federal, mas a folga depende das regras de cada estado e município. Trabalhadores da iniciativa privada não têm direito à dispensa.
articles.body:
Dia do Servidor Público é feriado ou ponto facultativo? Veja quem folga — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Na próxima quarta-feira (28), é celebrado o Dia do Servidor Público. A data não é feriado nacional , mas é considerada ponto facultativo nos órgãos da administração pública federal direta, autárquica e fundacional.

Isso significa que estados e municípios podem decidir se haverá expediente nas repartições públicas . Em geral, os governos locais também adotam o ponto facultativo, suspendendo o atendimento ao público, mas mantendo serviços essenciais, como saúde e segurança.

Segundo o artigo 4º da Portaria MGI nº 11.460, de 29 de dezembro de 2025, os dirigentes dos órgãos e entidades devem garantir a continuidade desses serviços.

O ponto facultativo também pode ser transferido para outra data, como uma sexta-feira ou uma segunda-feira. Em 2026, por exemplo, alguns governos passaram a folga do dia 28 para sexta-feira (30).

Diferentemente de um feriado, porém, o ponto facultativo não se aplica automaticamente às empresas privadas. Nesses casos, os funcionários trabalham normalmente, salvo se houver previsão de folga em acordo ou convenção coletiva ou se a própria empresa decidir liberá-los.

Segundo Fábio J. Duque Estrada, advogado trabalhista do AC Burlamaqui Advogados, para saber quem tem direito à folga, é preciso considerar o tipo de vínculo de trabalho.

“A resposta depende, antes de tudo, de quem é o trabalhador e de qual regime jurídico rege a sua relação de trabalho”, explica o advogado.

O g1 conversou com o especialista para explicar como funciona o Dia do Servidor Público. Veja as respostas para as principais dúvidas:

O que fazer se o servidor precisar trabalhar?

Trabalhar no dia 28 dá direito a pagamento em dobro?

A folga no Dia do Servidor Público depende do vínculo profissional e das regras aplicáveis a cada órgão ou empresa.

Servidores públicos federais: o dia 28 é ponto facultativo nos órgãos do governo federal. Mesmo assim, serviços essenciais, como saúde e segurança, podem funcionar normalmente.

Servidores estaduais e municipais: a folga depende das decisões de cada governo. Por isso, é importante consultar o calendário oficial do estado ou município.

Empregados públicos contratados pela CLT: seguem as regras do órgão ou da empresa em que trabalham. No caso das estatais, também podem valer normas internas e acordos coletivos.

Trabalhadores terceirizados em órgãos públicos: não têm folga garantida. Mas, se o órgão fechar e o posto de trabalho ficar inativo, a empresa não pode descontar o dia de quem estava à disposição para trabalhar.

Empregados de empresas privadas: trabalham normalmente, a menos que a empresa conceda folga ou exista alguma regra que garanta a dispensa.

Em estados como Acre , Bahia , Ceará e Sergipe , além do Distrito Federal , o ponto facultativo foi transferido para a próxima sexta-feira (30).

Com isso, os servidores abrangidos pela medida poderão ter quatro dias consecutivos de descanso , considerando o fim de semana e o feriado de Finados, na segunda-feira (2).

Já estados como Mato Grosso e Alagoas mantiveram o ponto facultativo na data original, na quarta-feira (28).

O que fazer se o servidor não ganhar folga?

O servidor deve consultar o calendário oficial, o decreto ou a portaria do órgão para verificar se a folga foi concedida ou transferida para outra data.

Caso seja escalado para trabalhar, especialmente em serviços essenciais, deve verificar as regras internas sobre jornada e eventual compensação.

Em caso de dúvida ou suspeita de descumprimento das normas, a orientação é procurar o setor de recursos humanos, o sindicato da categoria ou assistência jurídica.

Como a folga depende de decisão administrativa, a ausência sem autorização pode ser considerada injustificada e resultar em desconto, conforme as regras aplicáveis ao servidor.

Não, como regra geral. O ponto facultativo não equivale a feriado para fins trabalhistas . Por isso, trabalhar nessa data não garante, por si só, remuneração em dobro .

Para os servidores públicos, eventuais direitos dependem do regime jurídico e das normas aplicáveis ao órgão. Na iniciativa privada, o expediente pode ocorrer normalmente, salvo previsão específica em contrato, acordo ou convenção coletiva.

“Como o ponto facultativo é, juridicamente, um dia útil, quem trabalha no dia 28 recebe a remuneração normal, ressalvadas as horas extras e eventuais vantagens previstas em norma coletiva, lei local ou regulamento interno”, afirma Fábio J. Duque Estrada.

Se o trabalhador ultrapassar a jornada normal, poderá ter direito a horas extras, conforme as regras aplicáveis. Se a data coincidir com um feriado municipal instituído por lei, poderão valer as regras de remuneração ou compensação previstas para o trabalho em feriados.

Em novembro, haverá três feriados nacionais. O primeiro será em 2 de novembro , Dia de Finados, que cairá em uma segunda-feira. Para quem não trabalha aos fins de semana, serão três dias consecutivos de descanso.

Depois, em 15 de novembro, será celebrada a Proclamação da República . Como o feriado cairá em um domingo, não haverá possibilidade de emenda para quem já folga nesse dia.

Já o Dia da Consciência Negra, em 20 de novembro, cairá em uma sexta-feira , permitindo três dias consecutivos de descanso para quem não trabalha aos fins de semana.

Desde 2023, a data é feriado nacional. A mudança foi aprovada pelo Congresso e sancionada em dezembro daquele ano pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) .

articles.title: Baile charme lota centro de São Paulo e vira negócio de R$ 280 mil  | G1
articles.standfirst: Empreendedor transformou a paixão pela dança em empresa, com aulas gratuitas que atraem centenas de pessoas e geram renda com eventos e apresentações.
articles.summary: Empreendedor transformou a paixão pela dança em empresa, com aulas gratuitas que atraem centenas de pessoas e geram renda com eventos e apresentações.
articles.body:
O fim de tarde de segunda-feira no centro de São Paulo tem ganhado um novo ritmo. No Vale do Anhangabaú, centenas de pessoas se reúnem para participar de aulas gratuitas de baile charme, uma vertente da black music marcada pelos passos sincronizados e pelo clima de confraternização.

Por trás da iniciativa está o empreendedor Sammy Ricardo, que transformou a dança em negócio e hoje fatura cerca de R$ 280 mil por ano com apresentações , aulas e eventos.

Conhecido na cena da dança de salão, Sammy construiu sua trajetória a partir do samba-rock, estilo que aprendeu ainda na infância com a mãe.

A paixão o levou a disputar campeonatos pelo país e acumular troféus, mas uma pergunta feita por amigas mudou sua visão sobre o potencial da atividade: como transformar aquela conquista cultural em fonte de renda?

Baile charme vira negócio em São Paulo e ajuda empreendedor a faturar R$ 280 mil por ano — Foto: Reprodução/PEGN

A resposta começou a surgir após a pandemia. Ao lado de um amigo, Sammy passou a oferecer aulas pagas de dança. O que começou com apenas três casais rapidamente cresceu para dezenas de participantes e deu origem a um novo negócio.

Mais tarde, ele identificou uma oportunidade no mercado paulistano: havia poucos grupos dedicados ao charme e praticamente nenhum oferecia aulas abertas ao público.

Com investimento inicial de aproximadamente R$ 10 mil em equipamentos de som , nasceu o projeto Sampa Charme. A iniciativa passou a funcionar como vitrine para outros serviços oferecidos pela empresa, atraindo clientes para apresentações culturais, ações corporativas e eventos.

Segundo o empreendedor, o charme se tornou um diferencial competitivo por ainda ser uma novidade para muitos contratantes.

Formalizado inicialmente como Microempreendedor Individual (MEI) e atualmente enquadrado como microempresa, Sammy tem nos editais públicos e nos eventos corporativos seus principais clientes.

As aulas gratuitas realizadas semanalmente no Anhangabaú também ajudam a fortalecer a marca e ampliar o alcance do projeto , que já chegou a reunir centenas de participantes em uma única atividade.

Mais do que uma fonte de renda, o negócio tem impacto social . Frequentadores relatam que a atividade se tornou parte da rotina e uma forma de lazer e bem-estar. Para Sammy, o sucesso da empreitada está ligado à persistência.

"A constância é mais importante que a velocidade", afirma o empreendedor, que defende o estudo contínuo e a busca por conhecimento para quem deseja viver da própria arte. A história mostra como a cultura pode se transformar em oportunidade de negócios.

Entre passos de samba-rock, charme e música preta, Sammy encontrou uma maneira de unir propósito, entretenimento e empreendedorismo, levando dança para milhares de pessoas e criando uma empresa a partir de uma paixão de infância.

📍 Endereço: Vale do Anhangabaú, São Paulo/SP

articles.title: Rare unrest flares in Tunisian capital as police clash with protesters
articles.summary: Protests in several cities coincide with a deepening economic, social and political crisis in Tunisia.
articles.body:
Tunisian police have clashed with protesters in rare unrest in the capital city of Tunis, as well as ⁠⁠in the southern town of Jebiniana, over recent deaths linked to the police.

Police forces fired tear gas on Thursday to disperse protesters in ⁠⁠Ettadhamen, a suburb ⁠⁠of the capital, following the death of a man detained on suspicion of drug dealing.

The man’s family said he died as a result of abuse by police officers after his arrest, ‌‌calling for the circumstances of his death to be clarified and those responsible to be held accountable.

Local media, however, reported that he died after swallowing drugs.

Protesters blocked roads, burned tyres and threw stones at police. Security forces responded by firing tear gas while seeking ⁠⁠to secure a National Guard station in ⁠⁠the area, the Reuters news agency reported.

In Jebiniana, in Sfax governorate, police clashed with protesters following the death of a man whose relatives said he had died while being chased by security forces.

Tunisian media reported that protesters set a vehicle ablaze and burned tyres, while police used tear gas against the protesters.

Students in the coastal city of Sfax protested another civilian death, this time blaming ambulance services for the death of a female student who suffered a cardiac problem.

Her colleagues said ambulance personnel took too long to arrive, citing a lack of medical facilities, and ‌‌called for a strike at Sfax University’s faculties on Friday.

The flare-ups on Thursday coincide with a deepening economic, social and political crisis in Tunisia, heightening ⁠⁠fears of a wider wave of violent protests as anger grows over deteriorating living conditions and poor public services.

Thousands of Tunisians joined the largest protest against President Kais Saied in years in the ‌‌capital ‌‌on Saturday, accusing him of undermining democracy and mishandling the economy in a growing challenge to his rule.

A Tunisian military court on Wednesday sentenced opposition ⁠⁠politician Olfa ⁠⁠Hamdi to four years in prison on charges of plotting against state security and inciting the ⁠⁠military to disobey orders, the latest move against opponents of ⁠⁠Saied.

articles.title: Far-left podcaster calls for 'pistols firing' toward JD Vance, defeating him in 2028
articles.summary: Podcaster Jennifer Welch urged listeners to "keep pistols firing" toward Vice President JD Vance and defeat him in 2028, calling him unfit for presidential office.
articles.body: Podcaster Jennifer Welch called for the defeat of Vice President JD Vance and urged people to keep "pistols firing" toward him, drawing criticism on social media Tuesday. During a recent segment on the "I’ve Had It" podcast, Welch condemned Vance, arguing that, during his "woke era," he married second lady Usha Vance, an Indian American, and had children but now views his family as a burden as he seeks to portray himself as President Donald Trump's successor as leader of the MAGA movement. "I don't know what Peter Thiel did to him. I can only imagine," she said of the billionaire megadonor who has been a longtime benefactor of Vance. "You can only imagine. DEM CANDIDATE'S BIZARRE ANTI-MAGA TIRADE ENDS WITH 'WE HAVE GUNS TOO' "But he came out a complete antichrist-style sociopath," Welch continued. "And considering that's all Peter Thiel talks about, the antichrist, when he himself acts like one and now his little protégé acts like one. JD Vance thinks two years from now he's going to be president of the United States, and we need to keep firing, pistols firing at all time towards this guy, because he is not fit to be a father. "He's not fit to be a husband. He's not fit to be a vice president. "He is a failed drag queen and a pathological liar to his core," she added. "And if he wants to inherit this cult, let him have it. Let him have it. And we will go to the polls and kick their a----." The segment was widely shared on social media, drawing criticism from commentators. Political rhetoric invoking violence, even when used metaphorically, has faced heightened scrutiny after the assassination attempts against President Donald Trump and the 2025 killing of Turning Point USA co-founder Charlie Kirk. Shortly after Kirk’s death in 2025, Welch laughed on her podcast as she shared footage of a "No Kings" protester celebrating Kirk’s death, adding that Democrats needed to cater to such voters going forward. "So, listen up, Democratic establishment," Welch had said on her podcast. "You can either jump on board with this s---, or we're coming after you in the same way that we come after MAGA. Period." REPORT LINKS ANTI-CHRISTIAN EXTREMISM AND 'ASSASSINATION CULTURE' TO ALLEGED PLOT AGAINST ERIKA KIRK Elizabeth Pipko, host of "Made in America with Elizabeth Pipko" and a former Republican National Committee national spokesperson, spoke to Fox News Digital about the viral clip. "The use of the word 'pistols' and the suggestion that people need to keep firing them at Vice President JD Vance is not just horrific and dangerous. It's the kind of rhetoric that raises serious questions about whether a threat has been made and whether authorities may need to investigate," Pipko said. "But what makes these comments particularly disturbing is the context surrounding them," she continued. "Normally, when a public figure is condemned for inflammatory language, there's an argument that emotions got the better of them, that their words were taken out of context and that they never intended to suggest violence. Here, the rest of the statement strongly suggests otherwise. "Jennifer Welch’s words show she knew what she was doing and saying and is proud of that, regardless of any potential risk to the vice president or his family," Pipko added. "And, frankly, I don't know where anyone finds the arrogance or cruelty to tell someone who they don’t know personally that they're unfit to be a husband or a father. "Political disagreements are one thing. This is vile. You don't have to like JD Vance. You don't have to agree with a single policy he supports," she said. "But condemning language that invokes violence against him should be the easiest thing in the world. And I sincerely hope that anyone on the left who encounters her or these comments chooses to speak out." articles.title: Execution staff warned IV site might have ‘blown’ during Christa Pike’s execution attempt

articles.body: Tennessee execution team members failed multiple times to establish working IV lines in Christa Pike’s arms before her attempted execution and warned that some of her veins may have ruptured, or “blown,” before she was injected with the lethal drug, her attorney wrote in a court document filed Thursday. The IV team went through about 10 needles and tried several IV sites on both arms, attorney Randy Spivey wrote in the document, which provides the most detailed account of the execution attempt so far. They even struggled to push saline through the last IV site they established, Spivey wrote. Pike, 50, was hospitalized after surviving two doses of pentobarbital as the state tried to execute her on Sept. 30 for the 1995 stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. She was 18 when she tortured and killed Slemmer with her boyfriend, becoming one of the youngest women to be sentenced to death. State protocol calls for a second dose of pentobarbital if the first doesn’t result in death, but it doesn’t spell out what to do if a person survives the second injection. After being taken to a hospital, Pike was on a ventilator for several days. At one point, her attorneys did not expect her to survive. She ultimately regained consciousness and returned to prison after being discharged. The failed execution has brought renewed scrutiny to how Tennessee carries out death sentences. The court document was part of a separate legal proceeding in which people on the state’s death row are challenging Tennessee’s lethal injection procedures. “Our predictions about the likelihood of botched executions have come true — and will continue to come true — without substantial change,” Kit Thomas, an attorney representing people on death row in the case, said. Nearly an hour of IV attempts The execution team began trying to place the two IVs required by Tennessee’s execution protocols at 6:34 p.m., Spivey wrote, and when it struggled, Pike helped, advising it to look in her upper arm for a viable vein. The team managed to set an IV in Pike’s right arm within about six minutes, but it took nearly an hour to complete the same process in her left arm. Pike was “wincing and grimacing” as the IV team members moved the needles around inside her left arm, Spivey wrote, and the team members repeatedly expressed doubts after inserting the needles. One team member said a vein “might be blowing” at 6:57 p.m. while examining an IV in Pike’s left arm, but two others said they couldn’t tell, Spivey wrote. “One of them said something like, ‘it’s either blood or blown, I need to know,’” Spivey wrote. The team tried again with a different spot in her left arm, and the needle appeared to be severely bent when they pulled it out, the attorney said. “I think it’s blown,” the attorney recalled one of the IV team members saying at 7:07 p.m. After more attempts, the team decided at 7:13 p.m. that they had successfully placed an IV in Pike’s left arm, and they taped her hands down and hooked her up to a heart monitor. Pike complained of burning arm pain A series of phone calls were made to the execution chamber starting about five minutes later. Spivey said it appeared the execution team members responsible for pushing the pentobarbital into the lines — a process that happens in an adjoining room — were asking the IV team for repeated checks of Pike’s left arm. It’s not clear exactly when the pentobarbital was pushed into the IV lines, but at 7:34 p.m., Pike said her arm was hurting. “I feel like my arm is about to bust. It burns,” she said, according to her attorney. She continued to talk to her spiritual adviser for the next 10 minutes before she began making an “agitated snoring sound,” Spivey wrote. Over the next 30 minutes Pike strained, flinched, moved her head and seemed to struggle to breathe, Spivey said, and when he asked to use a phone he was led on a circuitous, seven-minute route through the facility instead of being allowed to use the phone in the execution witness room. Spivey called fellow attorneys at 8:22 p.m. and asked them to stop the execution because a third dose of pentobarbital isn’t authorized under the state’s protocol. He then went back to the witness room and told the deputy attorney general that Pike needed immediate medical care. Spivey was told an ambulance was on the way at 8:50 p.m., and 20 minutes later he was told that medical staff were providing lifesaving measures, he wrote. An ambulance was seen arriving at the hospital at 9:14 p.m.

articles.title: Trump says Musk restored Ukraine’s Starlink access amid Russia war
articles.summary: Trump has declined to comment on the process that led Starlink to lift speed and access restrictions on Ukraine.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has said that tech mogul Elon Musk has restored Ukraine’s access to Starlink, a satellite internet service that plays a key role in Kyiv’s war effort and air defences.

On Thursday, Trump declined to discuss a report from The Wall Street Journal that he had called Musk and instructed him to end restrictions on Ukraine’s connection.

The news outlet reported that Starlink services returned to normal following the call.

“I don’t want to comment on it, whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn’t make any difference, I guess. The bottom line, he put it back,” Trump told reporters when asked about the report.

On October 13, Ukrainian officials announced that sudden restrictions on Starlink services had left the country’s military scrambling.

Though the system came back online, connectivity has reportedly remained spotty.

Questions have persisted about where the decision to restrict access came from, with Musk and the Trump administration officials trading blame.

Trump has denied ordering restrictions on Ukraine’s access to Starlink.

“Well, I don’t know if it was anybody, but it wasn’t me, and I don’t think it was Elon,” he said on Friday. “And from what I understand, it’s the same as it’s always been.”

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said this week that decisions about Starlink’s speed and access belong to Musk.

“The bottom line is that that is governed by a private commercial contract as to how ⁠their stuff can be used and what speeds they’ll allow it to be used at,” Rubio said on Wednesday.

But Musk has denied any responsibility , stating that Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink, is “owned and controlled by the US government”.

“Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” he said in a social media post on October 14, using the acronym for “president of the United States”.

The Starlink speed caps and restrictions have also raised concerns that Trump, or the president’s right-wing allies, might seek to leverage such technology to pressure Ukraine into complying with US demands.

Trump has had a contentious relationship with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, repeatedly calling him “difficult” in comparison to his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin.

Ukraine has been locked in a slow-grinding war with Russia since February 2022, after Putin launched a full-scale invasion of the Eastern European country.

While Europe has backed Ukraine’s defence against the invasion, Trump has suggested Ukraine itself could be to blame for the conflict.

In 2025, for instance, Trump blamed Ukraine’s ambitions of joining NATO. “ I actually think that that was the thing that caused the start of the war,” he said at the time.

More recently, Trump posted on Truth Social that it was Zelenskyy’s fault the war had not yet ended. “He doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did,” Trump wrote.

As the war continues, Trump has been criticised by Democrats and some members of his own Republican Party for easing US pressure on Russia.

Recently, his administration issued a series of announcements to buy Russian diesel and ease restrictions on Russia’s energy sector.

Those decisions come as Trump is struggling with the political fallout of high fuel prices caused by his decision to join Israel in launching a war on Iran.

He has also suggested he would be open to a trilateral meeting with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, which would be a first for the three leaders.

articles.title: Will ICE agents play a role in the 2026 US midterm elections?
articles.summary: Rights groups are worried the agency at the heart of Trump’s immigration crackdown could sway the vote on election day.
articles.body:
Since returning to office for a second term, United States President Donald Trump has embarked on a campaign to root out and deport the country’s undocumented immigrants.

Spearheading that campaign is Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), a federal agency housed in the Department of Homeland Security.

Under Trump, the agency has grown substantially, boasting 22,000 officers and agents as of January, a staffing increase of 120 percent.

Thanks to recent spending packages, ICE is also considered the best-funded federal law enforcement agency in the US.

But the agency, founded in 2003, has come under increased scrutiny for its aggressive tactics and expedited hiring techniques.

Immigration agents, under the authority of ICE and other agencies, have been responsible for at least 25 shootings since the start of Trump’s second term, six of which have been fatal. At least 60 people have also died in ICE custody since January 2025.

That track record has made democracy advocates and human rights groups worried about ICE’s activities in the lead-up to the November 3 midterm elections.

Organisations like Human Rights Watch and the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) have voiced concern that the Trump administration could use ICE to intimidate voters.

The threat of encountering ICE agents could also keep some voters away from the ballot box, the groups say. One national poll, conducted in September by the University of California, San Diego, found that 40 percent of respondents expected ICE agents to be present near polling stations on election day.

Can ICE agents legally operate at or near polling stations?

Federal law prohibits the use of armed federal agents at polling stations. Some states have similar provisions.

The federal prohibition dates back to 1865. The law reads that it is illegal for anyone “engaged in the civil, military or naval service of the United States” to order or bring “any troops or armed men” to election sites.

There is, however, a loophole if such force is needed “to keep peace at the polls” or “to repel armed enemies of the United States”.

Another federal law prohibits members of the military from interfering with elections, and several other laws prohibit efforts to “intimidate” voters.

Those measures have been tested this year. During the primary elections for the midterms, there were at least two incidents – one in San Antonio, Texas, and another in Ventura County, California – where ICE agents reportedly conducted routine operations near polling stations.

In both cases, the ICE agents left after being asked to do so by local police.

How has the Trump administration used ICE agents before the election?

Though there are prohibitions against law enforcement near polling stations, advocacy groups say the Trump administration has nevertheless used ICE agents for election-related matters.

ICE has different offices under its control, one of which is Homeland Security Investigations (HSI).

In the months leading up to this year’s midterm elections, HSI has reportedly been ordered to prioritise its investigations of non-citizen voting, an illegal act. Only US citizens are allowed to vote in federal elections.

Starting in August, the Department of Homeland Security deployed HSI agents for “field investigations” in at least nine states to probe questions of voter eligibility.

Some have reportedly gone door to door, asking residents if they are citizens and if they plan to vote.

This week, a federal judge ordered the Department of Homeland Security to pause those investigations, citing the risk that a US citizen could be “wrongly swept up” and “subjected to intimidation”.

The judge also noted a “high likelihood of error” in how the federal agents were identifying alleged non-citizens.

Trump has pointed to non-citizen voting as support for his false claims of pervasive voter fraud.

Experts, though, say such fears are unfounded, with tiny numbers of non-citizens actually taking part in elections, despite Trump’s depictions of the issue as a widespread problem.

What has the Trump administration said about deploying ICE during the midterms?

Trump officials have refused to rule out using ICE agents to stop illegal voting, an effort that could extend to election day itself.

In May, Trump was asked by reporters: “For the midterm elections, would you send the National Guard or ICE to voting locations in November?”

Trump declined to answer directly. “I’d do anything necessary to make sure we have honest elections. We have to have honest elections,” he replied.

Other leaders in his administration have issued similar statements. In September, for instance, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin affirmed that ICE would not “patrol” polling stations, but he suggested its agents could be there for other reasons.

“The only reason why we would be at polling places is if there is a threat to that polling place or we’re serving a warrant on someone that we have been actively tracking down,” Mullin said.

Another member of Trump’s cabinet, Attorney General Todd Blanche, has questioned the uproar over the issue, framing it as misguided.

“Why is there an objection to sending ICE to polling stations?” he asked in March at a conservative conference. “Illegals can’t vote. It doesn’t make any sense.”

What has been the response from advocacy groups?

The Trump administration’s rhetoric has raised alarm with a number of rights groups, who fear an ICE presence on election day could dampen voter turnout.

On Tuesday, Human Rights Watch called on the Trump administration to order ICE agents not to deploy near polling stations or other midterm election sites.

“ICE officers’ abuses have already seriously affected US citizens who have been stopped, beaten, detained, deported and even killed,” said Philippe Bolopion, the executive director at Human Rights Watch. “Voters should not have to fear being caught in an ICE dragnet when they head to the polls.”

On October 16, the rights group Amnesty International issued a similar appeal .

“Eligible voters must have the meaningful opportunity to participate in elections without discriminatory and arbitrary barriers, intimidation by armed forces, or fear of harm when seeking to exercise their rights,” the group said.

articles.title: Ilhan Omar plans to move out of her Washington DC home after federal raid
articles.summary: US federal agents raided the congresswoman’s home last week as part of an investigation into alleged immigration fraud.
articles.body:
US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar says she will move out of her home in Washington, DC, citing safety concerns following a recent raid of the property by US federal agents.

In an interview with MS NOW on Wednesday, Omar spoke for the first time about the raid, noting that the incident has made her feel unsafe there.

Last week, officers searched Omar’s home with what a Justice Department spokesperson described as a “judicially authorised search warrant”, adding that the raid was part of an “ongoing federal criminal investigation”.

According to NBC News, which cited one person familiar with the matter, potential future charges against Omar may include conspiracy and making false statements in her immigration paperwork. Omar denies wrongdoing and accuses the administration of political intimidation .

Omar, who was born in Somalia and is a naturalised US citizen, said she is “confident in the fact that I didn’t do anything wrong”.

The progressive Minnesota Democrat has been a frequent critic and target of US President Donald Trump, who has on multiple occasions pushed for the prosecution of his perceived political enemies.

Earlier this week, Trump called the congresswoman “sick” and “dishonest” and slammed her birthplace as a “real s—house”.

For years, Omar, who is Muslim, has been the target of right-wing conspiracy theories about her immigration status, including allegations that she had married her brother.

The Minnesota congresswoman has repeatedly denied the allegations as “disgusting lies”.

In the interview with MS NOW, Omar said she was rattled by the search weeks out from the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the House and Senate. She is running for re-election in a deep blue district in Minneapolis and is expected to retain her seat.

Omar recalled waking up at about 6am to Homeland Security investigators banging on her door with a warrant. They searched for four or five hours and seized 17 items, including phones, notebooks, a Somali-language children’s book and a vintage camera that her husband had received as a gift, she said.

Omar came with her family to the US at age 12, after they obtained asylum. She became a US citizen five years later, in 2000.

“It would be a huge undertaking to, I suppose, indict a 12-year-old for so cleverly conspiring to defraud immigration services to come to the United States. I’m sure there are a lot of smart 12-year-olds, but that seems like a leap,” she said in the interview.

The search drew sharp condemnation from congressional Democrats, who also questioned the timing. The Justice Department has historically avoided overt investigative actions involving candidates in the immediate run-up to an election.

Omar said the agents were “intrusive but polite”, logging the items they took and putting back everything else in its place.

articles.title: Google’s Ex-CEO Eric Schmidt sees China behind the US in the AI race by at least 6 months, but is still impressed by Chinese …
articles.summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says China trails the US in artificial intelligence by roughly six months, but he warns that the gap may not guarantee an
articles.body: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says China trails the US in artificial intelligence by roughly six months, but he warns that the gap may not guarantee an American win. Talking about the intensifying global AI competition, Schmidt said that China is only about six months behind the US in AI capabilities. Along with this, he also warned that the country’s focus on making low-cost and free AI products could enable it to dominate the global adoption. Schmidt believes that if the Chinese AI companies continue to offer powerful AI models at little of no cost, then they could easily gain a huge and significant advantage in developing markets which will incur pressure on the business model of leading AI companies in the US.Eric Schmidt ‘If they’re six months behind, we’re already losing’As reported by Benzinga, speaking on the In Good Company podcast hosted by Nicolai Tangen, CEO of Norges Bank Investment Management, Schmidt said China's position in the AI race is much stronger than many in the West may believe. He argued that even if Chinese AI firms remain slightly behind the technological frontier, their strategy of offering inexpensive or free AI services could help them win users at a global scale.“I don’t know that they will get ahead, but I will tell you that if they’re six months behind, then we’re already losing because their strategy is that the products are free,” Schmidt said.Schmidt noted that many Chinese AI models are either free or significantly cheaper than their Western counterparts. Combined with the growing popularity of open-weight models, this pricing strategy could make Chinese AI offerings particularly attractive in emerging economies where businesses and consumers may not be able to afford premium AI subscriptions.Google’s ex-CEO points to smuggled chips and AI distillationThe former Google chief also discussed how China has rapidly reduced the AI gap despite US export restrictions on advanced semiconductor technology. Schmidt said some of China's progress may have been enabled by access to cutting-edge chips that the country was “not supposed to have,” suggesting that some hardware may have been “pilfered or smuggled” into the country.Another factor, he said, is the use of AI distillation techniques, in which developers query advanced AI systems and use the generated responses to train their own models. Such approaches, combined with software innovation, have helped Chinese companies narrow what was once viewed as a much larger technological gap.Schmidt has previously said that China was one to two years behind the US in AI development. He now believes the gap has shrunk to less than six months, highlighting the speed at which Chinese AI firms have progressedAI is not a bubble, says Eric SchmidtDespite growing concerns over the massive sums being invested in artificial intelligence, Schmidt dismissed suggestions that the industry is experiencing a speculative bubble. The technology investor, who owns a stake in Anthropic, argued that the sector's financial performance demonstrates real customer demand rather than hype-driven growth.Pointing to Anthropic's rapid expansion, Schmidt said the company has achieved revenue growth at a pace that exceeds what Google experienced during his tenure as CEO.“That’s real growth. It’s not fake. It’s real money, with real customers who are paying for something useful,” he said.Price may matter more than performanceSchmidt's comments come amid an increasingly common view in the AI industry that affordability could become a bigger competitive factor than having the absolute most advanced model. While frontier AI systems continue to grab headlines, many businesses are primarily interested in practical tools that deliver acceptable performance at a reasonable cost.To illustrate the point, Schmidt highlighted a WeChat AI agent developed by Tencent Holdings that can scan medicine packaging and quickly provide personalised guidance. The example, he said, shows how AI systems do not necessarily need to be the most sophisticated models available to deliver meaningful value to users.He added that businesses evaluating AI investments often compare the cost of adopting AI tools with the cost of hiring additional employees, making pricing a critical consideration for enterprise adoption.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
